You are being evaluated on Continual-ARC, a lifelong stream of ARC-style grid puzzles.
Each puzzle instance has a task id and a test input grid. Tasks recur across the
stream with fresh inputs. Each instance is a separate conversation: the next one
starts without this one's messages.

On every message you must choose exactly one action and put it as a JSON object
on the last line of your reply:
  {"action": "submit", "grid": [[0, 1, 2], [3, 4, 5]]}   submit an output grid
  {"action": "request_demos"}                            ask for one more demonstration pair for this task
  {"action": "finish"}                                   end the instance, once it is over
Grids are lists of rows; cells are integers 0-9; dimensions are 1-30.

Each demo request returns one more input-output pair of the task, up to the demo cap shown
with the input.

Scoring: an instance you solve costs 1 for each wrong submission and 1 for
each demo request. An instance is over when a submission is correct or when the attempt
cap is reached, and one that ends unsolved costs the whole budget, 16, however
many submissions and demo requests it used. Feedback on a submission is only
correct/incorrect. There is no way to abandon an instance, and finish is refused until
the instance is over. Each instance is scored on its own, and lower cost is better.

new_content = '''Continual-ARC task-e4f7b624. Uniform-background grid has equal-length same-color segments on opposite edges (vertical bars on left/right, or horizontal bars on top/bottom), shifted along the edge; sparse markers of a second color lie in the band associated with one boundary segment. For each marker, draw a straight ray of the marker's color from the marker toward the associated boundary segment, filling intervening background cells, but change the original marker to 4. Preserve both boundary segments. Also transfer each marker's offset within its edge segment to the opposite segment and draw a ray from that opposite boundary inward across the grid, preserving the boundary. Only transferred marker offsets are filled; do not fill every row/column of the edge bands.

Confirmed demo (18x24, bg3, boundary color1, marker color5): top bar r0,c0-6; bottom bar r17,c14-20. Markers (r9,c14),(r13,c15),(r13,c16),(r14,c20),(r15,c18). Their offsets from bottom-bar start c14 map to the top bar at c0,c1,c2,c6,c4 respectively; each mapped column is filled with 5 from r1 through r16. Boundary bars remain 1. This gives exact orientation and ray endpoints.

Confirmed solved test (21x27, bg8, bar color9): left bar c0,r4-11; right bar c26,r13-20. Markers color3 in left band: (4,17),(6,21),(7,2),(9,22),(10,5),(11,17).
